items.evidence: Process scheduling is how the OS decides which process gets the CPU at any given time.
items.note: The student explains the basic concept but fails to mention the ready queue.
The student did not mention non-preemptive scheduling.
The student did not mention preemptive scheduling.
The student did not explain alternating CPU bursts and I/O waits.

items.evidence: First-Come First-Served where jobs are handled strictly in the order they arrive in the ready queue.
items.note: The student correctly describes FCFS as running processes in arrival order.
The student did not mention the convoy effect or its impact on wait time.

items.evidence: Shortest Job First, which picks the process with the smallest total execution time
items.note: The student incorrectly states it uses total execution time instead of the upcoming CPU burst.
The student did not define starvation.
The student did not mention aging.

target_reason: Correcting the misunderstanding about how Shortest Job First measures process length is crucial for accurate scheduling behavior.
target_focus: how the system measures the length of the next process
